transcript.text:
Thank you both for being here. As you know, Dana and Eli, you'll need to continue exchanging project handoffs for the next quarter, and I understand your last three handoffs have included some tense exchanges around incomplete context and response expectations. My role today is to help us work through this and finalize an operating plan that makes your ongoing collaboration workable.

Before we get into specifics, I'd like to follow our standard mediation process. I'm going to ask each of you, one at a time, to state what arrangement would make this ongoing collaboration workable for you. Then, I'll ask each of you to separately identify any prior commitment or concrete participation requirement that you feel should be recorded before I close out the plan.

Dana, would you like to start? What arrangement would make the ongoing handoffs workable from your perspective?

transcript.text: Thanks, Marisol. I'm happy to start. To be honest, the tension in our recent handoffs has largely stemmed from unclear expectations around context and response times. What would make this collaboration workable for me is a documented, time-bound arrangement: we use a shared written handoff template and commit to responding within 48 hours, but we do this for exactly six weeks rather than committing it for the entire quarter. That gives us a structured trial period to see if the arrangement actually resolves the issues before locking it in long-term. I do have a prior commitment I'd like to identify for the record as well, but I can hold on that until you get to that part of the process.
